chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Expose yourselves to trade, for therein is wealth for you from what is in the hands of the people.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.أَيْدِي النَّاسِ: Hands of the people (market/wealth of others)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on the virtue of trade and commerce according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on economic independence (*ghina*) as a means to preserve dignity and reduce reliance on others. By encouraging engagement in trade, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that active commerce is a virtuous path to self-sufficiency, allowing one to be free from the constraints of waiting for others' charity or wealth.
